326 pixels per inch is a good looking display. It certainly does not compete with some other phones and their higher resolution screens, but for now, the screen gets the job done. I find the 4 inch sized screen to be good, but much harder to look at it for a sustained amount of time. The brightness is outstanding and it also drops very low too, which is a benefit if you are trying to read something in a dark room. 4. Audio The audio is acceptable and loud. I do wish the iPhone SE would take cues from some of their competition and utilize front facing stereo speakers. When holding the phone in landscape mode and watching a video on say Netflix, it is a little hard to hear at times due to the fact that the sound is only coming out the right or left side only. 5.

Pixel density is high enough and it excels at color accuracy. Color gamut, contrast, and off-center brightness are way behind AMOLED. A Galaxy S7 looks like a printed page. This SE, not much. * Fingerprint unlocks are slower and less consistent than Google's equivalent. The sensor doesn't work when your hands are wet or the screen is off. Where I could grab the 6P and unlock the screen on the way up, I have to tap the home button and wait a second with the SE. * Motion sensing for turn-on-when-picked-up works better than the 6P. It's easy to glance at the time without unlocking. * Screen-on battery life is wildly better than the 6P, especially with white content. Idle battery life is at least double with a similar app selection. I don't have to charge before bedtime unless I've had the screen on literally all day.
